items.front: Net effect of two successive percentage changes a% then b%?
items.back: net = a + b + ab/100 (use + for rise, − for fall). Equal +x% then −x% gives −x²/100 % (never 0).
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Successive Percentage Change

items.front: If A is x% more than B, how much % less is B than A?
items.back: B is x/(100+x)×100 % less than A. (25% more means 20% less.) Price up x% means cut consumption by x/(100+x)×100 %.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Comparison of Percentage

items.front: Simple Interest formula and the doubling condition?
items.back: SI = PRT/100; Amount = P(1+RT/100). A sum doubles when RT = 100; becomes n times when RT = (n−1)×100.

items.front: Compound Interest formula; half-yearly & quarterly adjustments?
items.back: A = P(1+R/100)ⁿ; CI = A−P. Half-yearly: rate R/2, periods 2n. Quarterly: rate R/4, periods 4n.

items.front: CI − SI difference for 2 and 3 years (same P, R, T)?
items.back: 2 years: P(R/100)². 3 years: P(R/100)²×(3 + R/100). Year-1 CI = SI; CI exceeds SI from year 2.

items.front: Profit/Loss and discount — which base for each?
items.back: Profit%/Loss% are on CP: SP = CP(1±%/100). Discount is on MP: SP = MP(1−d/100). Never subtract discount% from mark-up%.

items.front: Two successive discounts a%, b% as a single discount?
items.back: Single equivalent = a + b − ab/100 (i.e. multiply (1−a/100)(1−b/100)).

items.front: Dishonest dealer selling at CP with a false weight — gain%?
items.back: gain% = error/(true value − error) × 100. A 900 g 'kg' gives 100/900 = 11.11%.

items.front: Two articles at the SAME selling price, one +x% one −x% — net result?
items.back: Always a net LOSS of x²/100 %, regardless of the actual price.
items.examPoint: Two articles same SP, equal profit% & loss%

items.back: Share ∝ Capital × Time (capital-months). Equal time means the capital ratio. Form C₁T₁:C₂T₂:…, take each fraction of profit.
items.examPoint: Partnership — profit sharing by capital × time

items.front: Alligation — ratio to blend two ingredients to a mean price m?
items.back: qty cheaper : qty dearer = (dearer − m) : (m − cheaper). Mean lies nearer the larger-quantity ingredient.
items.examPoint: Mixture & alligation — ratio for a target mean price

items.front: x% of A = y% of B — what is the ratio A : B?
items.back: A : B = y : x (cross-multiply xA/100 = yB/100).
items.examPoint: Percentage equality — x% of A = y% of B
